author: volume_calendar
note: Predicates 98/99/100. bars[0] is the reference (most recently closed) bar; index increases going back in time. VOLUME_CLIMAX reads bars 0..21 (volume avg over 1..20, ATR over 1..21). The default filler makes every padded bar identical (range 2.0, close 100, tick_volume 1000) so vavg=1000 and atr20=2.0 are exact. The two calendar predicates read ONLY b.time[0], set via anchor_date; their bar shape is inert.

fixtures.rationale: A volume climax is a blow-off/capitulation bar: an extreme surge in participation printed on an unusually wide price move. Filler bars each carry tick_volume 1000 (avg 1000) and range 2.0 (atr20 2.0). Bar0 has tick_volume 5000 (5x the average) and range 7.0 (3.5x atr20). Both the volume surge and the wide range are present, so it is a climax.

Volume surges to 5000 (5x the 1000 average) but the bar barely moves: range 1.2 against an atr20 of 2.0. Heavy volume inside a tight range is absorption/churn, not a climactic blow-off. A climax requires the price to travel far, so this is not one. (Attacks the wide-range clause.)

Range is wide (7.0, 3.5x atr20) but tick_volume is 1000, exactly the recent average. A wide bar on ordinary participation is a routine directional move; the defining feature of a climax is the volume blow-off, which is absent here. (Attacks the volume-surge clause.)

A perfectly unremarkable bar: range 2.0 (equal to atr20) and tick_volume 1200 (1.2x the 1000 average). Neither the price expansion nor the volume surge that define a climax is present, so both clauses fail.

vavg is 1000 so the tick_volume[0] > 3*vavg gate sits at 3000. tick_volume 3300 is 10% above 3000, inside the surge threshold. Range stays wide (7.0 vs atr20 2.0) so this isolates the volume clause. Not placed exactly on 3000.

Identical wide bar (range 7.0) but tick_volume 2700 is 10% below the 3000 surge threshold (3*vavg), outside it. Only the volume value changes from the inside case, so a false result pins the rejection to the volume clause.

atr20 is 2.0 so the r0 > 1.5*atr20 gate sits at 3.0. Bar0 range is 3.3 (103.3-100.0), 10% above 3.0, inside the wide-range threshold. Volume held high at 5000 (>3000) so this isolates the range clause. Not placed exactly on 3.0.
Range is 2.7 (102.7-100.0), 10% below the 3.0 wide-range threshold (1.5*atr20), outside it. Volume stays high at 5000 so a false result pins the rejection to the range clause alone.

2026-01-16 is a Friday and the third Friday of January 2026 (Fridays fall on the 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd, 30th). The third Friday is the monthly options/index-futures expiration, which is exactly what this predicate marks, so it must fire.

2026-05-08 is a Friday but the SECOND Friday of May 2026 (Fridays on the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, 29th). It is a Friday yet not the third, so a predicate that means 'third Friday' must not fire. (Attacks the which-Friday selection.)

2026-08-28 is a Friday but the FOURTH Friday of August 2026 (Fridays on the 7th, 14th, 21st, 28th). A Friday later than the third must not be reported as the third Friday. (Attacks the which-Friday selection from the other side.)

2026-05-18 is a Monday whose day-of-month (18) sits inside the 15-21 window, but it is not a Friday. Only a Friday can be the third Friday, so the day-of-week requirement must reject this. (Attacks the Friday clause independently of the day range.)

The implementation gates on day >= 15. 2026-05-15 is a Friday on day 15, on/above the lower edge and therefore inside the window. Day-of-month is an integer comparison so the edge value is exact and reliably included; paired with the day-14 case it brackets the lower bound.

2026-08-14 is a Friday on day 14, one below the day >= 15 lower edge and therefore outside the window. It differs from the day-15 inside case only in the day-of-month, so a false result pins the rejection to the lower-bound clause.

The implementation gates on day <= 21. 2026-08-21 is a Friday on day 21, on/within the upper edge and therefore inside the window. Integer day comparison makes the edge exact; paired with the day-22 case it brackets the upper bound.

2026-05-22 is a Friday on day 22, one beyond the day <= 21 upper edge and therefore outside the window. Only the day-of-month differs from the day-21 inside case, pinning the rejection to the upper-bound clause.

2026-03-31 is the last calendar day of Q1 (March 31, a trading Tuesday). This is the genuine quarter-end where index rebalancing and window-dressing concentrate, exactly what the predicate names, so it must fire.
2026-06-30 is the last calendar day of Q2 (June has 30 days). The genuine quarter-end must fire.
2026-09-30 is the last calendar day of Q3 (September has 30 days). The genuine quarter-end must fire.
2026-12-31 is the last calendar day of Q4 (December 31). The genuine year/quarter-end must fire.
2026-01-31 is the last day of January, but January does not end a quarter. The last day of a non-quarter month is not a quarter-end, so this must not fire. (Attacks the quarter-month clause.)

2026-04-30 is the last day of April, a late day-of-month, but April is the first month of Q2, not its end. A month-end of a non-quarter-closing month is not a quarter-end. (Attacks the quarter-month clause from a late day-of-month.)

2026-03-27 is a Friday four days before the Q1 close on March 31. It is NOT within the last two calendar days of the quarter, so the correct answer is false. The repaired predicate (quarter_month && day >= last_day-1, i.e. day >= 30 for March) returns false here, no longer mislabeling an ordinary late-March day as quarter-end. (Regression guard on the former day>=24 over-fire.)

2026-09-26 is four days before the Q3 close on September 30 and is not within the last two calendar days of the quarter, so the correct answer is false. The repaired predicate returns false (September has 30 days, so day 26 < 29 = last_day-1), no longer over-firing on ordinary late-quarter-month days. (Regression guard across a second quarter.)

The repaired predicate admits the last two calendar days of a quarter month: day >= last_day-1. March has 31 days, so the cutoff is day 30. 2026-03-30 (March, day 30) is on the lower edge, inside the admitted range, so it returns true. Integer day comparison makes the edge exact; paired with the day-29 case it brackets the threshold.

2026-03-29 (March, day 29) is one below the day >= last_day-1 cutoff of 30, outside the admitted range, so it returns false. Differs from the day-30 inside case only in day-of-month, bracketing the last-two-days threshold from below.
